thread:
Sam King: Heads-up: saw a near-OOM cluster event in euw2 ~11:40UTC. Allocator couldn't place new pods for ~3m, several requests got 503s. GPU pack usage hit 98% and KV cache thrash spiked. Link: https://dash.internal/redwood/euw2/allocator?range=15m
Priya Patel: timeline? what changed before 11:40? any deploys or traffic spikes?
Sam King: No code deploys. Traffic +15% in 10m due to a partner test, but the big signal was long-context jobs from a single tenant — median seq_len jumped 3x. Autoscaler reacted but allocator backlog grew.
Dmitri Ivanov: Checked node logs. Allocator loop experienced backlog and then hit per-node pod cap. Error sample: `allocator: failed_to_place: no-suitable-node (resources_available=false)`
Maya Lopez: KV cache eviction rate also skyrocketed which increased per-token work and memory per-request. We saw per-pod RSS go from 12GB to 18GB on some model servers.
EngOncall: infra-bot notified and we fried a couple of low-priority preemptible pools to egress headroom, that allowed short-term placement. autoscaler-bot: scaled +12 pods over 2m at 11:42:34 UTC.
autoscaler-bot: action: scaled_group(gpu-euw2-qlow) target=+12 current=58 -> 70, scale_time=120s
Priya Patel: Can we confirm why allocator waited vs falling back to compatible model variant? We have fallback rules for critical routes.
Dmitri Ivanov: Fallback was blocked because routing policy for that tenant is pinned to a high-memory quantized variant. Policy requires manual override for fallback to smaller model.
Sam King: Sequence: tenant spike -> KV cache evict -> per-pod memory bump -> allocator can't place (per-node caps hit) -> autoscaler started but provisioning + kube scheduling added ~2m delay -> some requests timed out.
Maya Lopez: Short-term mitigations we applied: lowered prefix retention from 10m -> 2m, reduced per-tenant concurrent requests from 20 -> 8, and temporarily unpinned the tenant routing to allow fallback to quantized-llama-7b. That dropped memory footprint 35% and recovered steady state.
Dmitri Ivanov: Suggestion: add automatic small-model-fallback when cluster headroom < 10% and request latency > 500ms for 30s. Also tune allocator to prefer spreading across AZs earlier rather than filling one AZ.
Priya Patel: Also need forecasting fix: modeling didn't predict the short burst because tenant's rolling average smoothed the spike. We should add a high-frequency signal source for 1-5m windows.
Sam King: Cost note: short-term scale +12 nodes (spot) cost ~ $1.8k for the burst window. If this becomes common, aggregated burst cost will dent margin.
Maya Lopez: Action items I propose: 1) autoscaler: reduce provisioning cooldown from 3m->90s for gpu pools; 2) allocator: implement soft-fallback rule; 3) forecasting: add 1-5m anomaly detector; 4) KV cache: dynamic retention based on LRU pressure.
Dmitri Ivanov: I'll open infra PR for allocator spread-by-az and soft-fallback policy (estim ETA: 3d).
Priya Patel: I'll update the forecasting model and add alert: "spike_1m_vs_15m > 2x" to fire to capacity oncall.
EngOncall: Recording incident notes and linking metrics: https://incidents.internal/1923456789
Sam King: Post-incident: keep a watch on euw2 for 24h, especially tenant X's request patterns. If we see >2 similar spikes, we schedule a deeper runbook and quota re-eval.
Maya Lopez: Quick config diff we applied (snippet):
```
replica.provisioning.cooldown: 180s -> 90s
kv.prefix_retention_secs: 600 -> 120
tenantX.concurrent_limit: 20 -> 8
```
Sam King: TL;DR: near-oom caused by mismatch of short-timescale spike + pinned routing + KV cache pressure. Mitigations worked, but we need autoscaler/allocator/forecasting improvements to avoid recurring cost/availability impact. :thumbsup:
Priya Patel: +1. I'll turn the alert into an SLO guard so product teams get notified before availability drops.
Dmitri Ivanov: Filing the allocator bug and linking to infra PR.
infra-bot: node-reboot (gpu-euw2-003) at 11:45 UTC by EngOncall — reason: reclaimed preemptible pool.
EngOncall: closing for now, ping if regressions.
